# Site Recovery
Laboratory work occasionally produces accidents. When it does, Security restores the site to normal and makes sure the accident leaves no trace. These procedures apply after any incident involving research, specimens or casualties, and they begin as soon as the area is safe.
## Scene Control - The area stays sealed until recovery is complete. Only Security, the Lead Researcher and the senior employee may enter. - Nobody outside the Company is allowed near the scene, including colonial medical staff and law enforcement. - Officers record what they found before anything is moved, and hand the record to the Sergeant.
## Hazards - Specimen remains, tissue and blood are handled only by officers in gloves and protective gear. Acid blood stays active after death. - Remains are bagged and handed to the Lead Researcher. Anything the Lead Researcher doesn't want is incinerated. - Acid damage, scorch marks and blood are cleaned or covered before the area is reopened. - Anyone exposed during the incident is sent to medical staff and reported to the Lead Researcher.
## Casualties - Company casualties are recovered, identified and reported to the senior employee. - Casualties are not discussed outside the Company until the senior employee has approved what is said. - The bodies of non-Company persons involved in a Category 4 or 5 incident are handled as the senior employee directs.
## Records - All recordings of the incident are collected, including camera footage, personal recorders and anything taken from witnesses. - Logs, reports and records that mention the incident are passed to the senior employee, who decides what is kept. - The official record states the approved explanation. It does not state what happened.
## Approved Explanations When colonists ask what happened, officers are to give one of these, as directed by the senior employee: - a gas leak or chemical spill; - an electrical fault or fire; - structural failure; - an attack by local wildlife; - a criminal act by persons unknown.
Officers are never to give a different explanation, add detail of their own, or admit there is anything else to explain.
## Witnesses - Company staff who saw the incident are reminded of their confidentiality obligations and given the approved explanation. - Witnesses outside the Company are handled as their category requires (see [textlink="Incident Response" link="CMUHandbookSecurityIncidents"/]). - Officers record every person who was present, and what they are likely to have seen.
